title: He got close enough to ask the right question.
paragraphs:
He got close enough to ask the right question.
Close enough to look holy.
Close enough to touch the doorway of eternal life.

Luke 18:18–23 gives us one of the saddest moments in Scripture. A ruler comes to Jesus with clean language, religious posture, and moral confidence: “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?” He wanted eternity. He just did not want to lose his idol to get it.
Jesus exposed the wound beneath the wealth.

The man could name commandments. He could talk morality. He could stand near Christ without surrendering to Christ. But when Jesus said, in effect, “Lay down the one thing sitting on the throne of your heart, then follow Me,” the mask split open. His money was not just in his hand. His money had wrapped itself around his soul.
And that is the terror of this text.

You can be near Jesus and still resist Him.
You can admire Jesus and still not obey Him.
You can ask eternal questions while protecting temporary gods.

The ruler touched the conversation.
He never touched grace by faith.
Because healing is not found in proximity to Jesus alone. It is found in surrender to Jesus as Lord.

But here’s what we miss: Jesus was not trying to ruin the man. Jesus was trying to free him. The command to sell was not cruelty. It was mercy with a blade. Christ was cutting away the cancer the man called treasure.
That is what Jesus still does.

He puts His finger on the one thing we do not want to release. The secret relationship. The ambition. The image. The addiction. The money. The pride. And when He does, it is not because He hates us. It is because He loves us too much to leave us chained to what cannot save.

The rich ruler went away sorrowful because he had great possessions.
The tragedy is deeper than that.
His possessions had him.

Friend, the Gospel is not “try harder and keep more rules.” The Gospel is that we are too bound, too proud, too sinful to save ourselves—but Jesus came for idolaters like us. He lived the righteous life we failed to live, died the death our sins deserved, and rose again to break the power of every false god. Salvation is not bought with gold. It is received by grace through faith in Christ alone.

So the question is not, “Have you come near Jesus?”
The question is, “Have you yielded everything to Him?”

Bring Him the thing you keep defending.
Bring Him the throne you do not want to vacate.
Bring Him your sorrow, your chains, your divided heart.
Because the hands that ask you to let go are the same hands that were pierced to save you.
